title: Text analysis techniques
learningObjective: Describe keyword (key phrase) extraction, entity detection, sentiment analysis and summarization, and related techniques such as PII detection and language detection.
foundation: Key phrase (keyword) extraction lists the main topics in a text: 'battery life', 'screen'.
Entity detection (named entity recognition, NER) finds and categorises things: people, places, organisations, products, dates, quantities.
Sentiment analysis says whether text is positive, negative, neutral or mixed, with confidence scores. Opinion mining links feelings to specific things: 'battery: positive, screen: negative'.
Summarization shortens text. Extractive summarization picks the most important sentences; abstractive summarization writes new sentences.
engineer: Azure Language in Foundry Tools provides prebuilt features: key phrase extraction, named entity recognition (categories and subcategories), entity linking (to Wikipedia entries), sentiment analysis with opinion mining (document- and sentence-level scores for positive, neutral, negative; label mixed), PII detection and redaction (text and conversations), language detection, extractive and abstractive summarization (documents and conversations), plus custom features (custom classification, custom NER, conversational language understanding).
Outputs include confidence scores you can threshold. Inputs are sent as documents in batches with IDs and optional language hints.

Alternatively, prompt a generative model to perform the same tasks with structured (JSON) output. Models are flexible (custom definitions, any wording) but less consistent and usually more expensive per item than prebuilt features.
Common pipeline: detect language → redact PII → sentiment and key phrases → store results for dashboards.

example.title: Understanding 50,000 reviews
body: A phone maker runs reviews through Azure Language: key phrases show 'battery life' and 'screen' dominate; opinion mining shows battery is positive and screen negative.
NER pulls out model names and store locations; abstractive summarization gives product managers a one-paragraph digest per model each week.

prerequisites: An Azure subscription with access to Microsoft Foundry (ai.azure.com)
permissions: Azure AI User or Cognitive Services User
limits: Model availability differs by region and deployment type
Deployments have tokens-per-minute (TPM) rate limits and quota per subscription and region
portal: Foundry portal > Language playground: paste text and try sentiment, NER, key phrases, PII and summarization.
Note the confidence scores and categories in the JSON output.

troubleshooting.cause: Reviews praise and criticise different features.
troubleshooting.fix: Use opinion mining for aspect-level sentiment.

troubleshooting.symptom: Entities are missed in short texts.
troubleshooting.cause: Wrong language or too little context.
troubleshooting.fix: Pass the correct language hint; check confidence scores.

comparisons.difference: Key phrases are main talking points; entities are categorised items (Person, Location).
Extractive selects existing sentences; abstractive writes new ones.

misconceptions.myth: Sentiment analysis only returns positive or negative.
misconceptions.reality: Also neutral and mixed, with scores.

misconceptions.myth: NER and PII detection are the same.
misconceptions.reality: PII detection focuses on personal data and can redact it.

architectureDecisions: Use prebuilt Azure Language features for consistent, scored results.
Use a model with JSON output for custom definitions.
